label: lad-6eb46
summary: The network scores a Connect-4 position for x with four board-pattern detectors (ReLU units over the board squares) whose values add, each with a positive weight, on the logit of the predicted chance that x wins; it reaches a training AUC of 0.884. The most important detector, xRaisedInCentre (switching it off gives an AUC of 0.769), rewards x's pieces on the second and third rows of the central columns over o's pieces on the bottom-left, and acts on 13.4% of the 449 positions with x on a1, b1 and c1. xOwnsCentreColumn rewards x on d1, d2 and d3, leftXRightO rewards x on the left-centre of the bottom row against o on e1, f1 and g1, and columnCOverBottomLeft rewards x on c2 and c3 over o on a1 and b1. In constructed boards, swapping o for x on d1 and d2 moves the predicted chance that x wins from 47% to above 99%.

resisted: Each unit is a weighted sum over the board, so its reading names the squares that dominate it and leaves out the small terms: the smaller weights (for example o on the upper rows pushing leftXRightO up) are described by the closed form but not explained. leftXRightO is a partial reading: the left-against-right bottom-row pattern holds in the self-probe and on the training positions (it acts on 98.2% of the 2600 positions with o on f1 and g1), but it still acts on 34.2% of the 11639 positions with x on f1. The readings are about territory (the centre column, raised central squares, the left-centre of the bottom row), not about lines of four or threats; whether a unit tracks threats was not tested with the query tools.

Notes: a composition's subgraph_nodes must exclude the children's nodes (the root lists only the output node, with the children's entries as its entries). get_formula returns no provenance id, so the analytical_formula records carry its LaTeX as payload. xn.py --recheck --record needs the record file to exist first.

refuted_and_fixed: columnCOverBottomLeft: the first hypothesis said the unit is off when x holds a1 and b1; the probe (x on c2, c3) left it on at a lower value, so the text now gives the share of training positions with x on a1 and b1 where it acts

accuracy.notes: numbers = placeholders plus the three literals of the input encoding (x = +1, o = -1, blank = 0) in the columnCOverBottomLeft hypothesis, which are not computed values. The root closed form (analytical_formula evidence) is rounded and carries no stated tolerance (counted as other).

leaves.name: columnCOverBottomLeft
leaves.why: Fires when x has built column c above the bottom row (c2, c3) over o's bottom-left corner pieces (a1, b1); the probes and the share of training positions where it acts with x versus o on these squares confirm it.

leaves.name: leftXRightO
leaves.why: Rewards x on the left-centre of the bottom row against o on the right bottom squares, confirmed by the probe on b1 and f1, but it still acts on many positions with x on f1 and its many small upper-row weights are not explained.

leaves.name: xRaisedInCentre
leaves.why: Large when x's pieces sit on the second and third rows of the central columns above o's bottom-left pieces and mostly off when x spent its pieces on a1, b1 and c1; the probe on d2 and e2 and the subgroups confirm it.

leaves.name: xOwnsCentreColumn
leaves.why: Fires when x holds the low squares of the centre column d and is off with o on d1 and d2 in the probe; it acts on every training position with x on d1, d2 and d3.

overall_function: The network adds four territory scores for x on the logit scale: x holding the low squares of the centre column, x's pieces raised on the second and third rows of the central columns over o's pieces on the bottom-left, x on the left-centre of the bottom row with o pushed to the right bottom squares, and x stacked on column c over o's bottom-left corner. Each score is a ReLU threshold of a weighted count of x-minus-o over the squares, so it switches on when its pattern is strong enough, and a firing score raises the chance that x wins (its output weight is positive); the scores do not gate each other and interact only through sharing the same squares. Holding the rarely filled squares of rows four to six at their training mean costs a little AUC, so most of the prediction comes from the bottom three rows. The probes did not test whether any unit tracks lines of four or threats; the readings are about territory.
stuck: Nothing blocked. Composition syntax (children's nodes must not be relisted) took one retry. Leaf meaning was the slow part: each unit is a dense weighted sum over the board, so the readings name the dominant squares and leftXRightO stays partial.
